## Introduction

In this post, I use R and Python together in the same Quarto document. I first calculate a summary statistic in R and then pass that result to Python using the `reticulate` package.

Data: [Palmer Penguins](https://allisonhorst.github.io/palmerpenguins/), Palmer Station Antarctica LTER.

## Calculate a value in R

First, I use R to calculate the average body mass of the penguins after removing missing values.

```{r}
#| message: false
#| warning: false

library(palmerpenguins)
library(reticulate)

average_mass <- mean(penguins$body_mass_g, na.rm = TRUE)

average_mass
```

The object `average_mass` is now an R object containing the mean body mass of the penguins.

## Use the R result in Python

Next, Python accesses the R object through `r.average_mass`. This means the value calculated in R is being used directly by Python.

```{python}
average_mass_from_r = r.average_mass

average_mass_from_r
```

## Perform another calculation in Python

Python now uses the value received from R to convert the average body mass from grams to kilograms.

```{python}
average_mass_kg = average_mass_from_r / 1000

average_mass_kg
```

The result demonstrates communication between the two languages: the average body mass was calculated in R, passed to Python, and then converted from grams to kilograms in Python.
